spinAero.shadowKSource: Geometric helical shadow depth (TailWake.GeometricShadow): the share of dynamic pressure a fully shadowed strip loses. Replaces the Report 648 wake correlation for EVERY surface of this type, and brings in the fuselage's own shadow on the tail and the wings (TailWake.BodyStation). Ty 2026-11-08: "expand the shadow work to all 6 shipping aircraft include the shadow effects of the fuselage on the tail and wing's too". 0.5 is the depth fitted on the Pitts against the owner's spin attitudes on 2026-11-08, and it is a PHYSICAL statement - half the q is gone where a wake fully covers a section - rather than a per-type fudge, so the six carry the same number until a type's own evidence moves it. What differs between types is the geometry, which is the point: the Pitts' cellule shadows itself, the Extra's stabiliser spans well outside its fuselage and is barely shadowed at all (measured in a tumble: tail q 1.00 -> 0.96), and the fuselage's own shadow is what takes the fin in an upright flat spin while leaving it in clear air inverted.
spinAero.controlSpoilerKSource: A deflected control on a BROADSIDE surface acts as a spoiler on the separated wake, not as a flap: adds k*sin(delta)*|sin(alpha_chord)|*q*S normal to the FIXED surface's own plane, over hinged tail strips only, ramped in over 20 deg from controlSpoilerOnsetDeg. 0.6 is the PITTS' value and is carried unchanged, not refitted per type: it was fitted there on 2026-11-10 to Ty flying a clip of his own Pitts flat spin ("the elevator literally does nothing in the spin"), and pitts-s2b-like.json holds the sweep it came from - elevator authority at alpha 80 of 3.7 deg/s2 at k 0, 15.5 at 0.3, 27.4 at 0.6, 43.4 at 1.0, where 1.0 leaves the curve nearly flat from 30 to 90 deg and a plate should not be. WHY THIS TYPE HAS IT NOW. It shipped on the Pitts and the Extra alone, and that was STAGING rather than a finding: the argument for the term is about the SECTION - post-stall the section law is Cd_max*sin(theta), which is flat at broadside, so a strip model gives a control on a broadside surface a direction to point its force in and no magnitude to command - and when this type's horizontal tail became a flat plate on 2026-11-10 (b7396cd0: stall 9 deg, Cl_max 0.90, blend 44) that argument started applying to it too. Worse, the controlSpoilerOnsetDeg 10 that came with the plate was INERT here, because the spoiler block in AeroModel.Compute is gated on controlSpoilerK > 0.0: the onset was moving the start of a term multiplied by zero, and the hole it was meant to close was being closed by the 44 deg blend alone. Ty 2026-11-10, shown exactly that and the argument that the restriction to two types was staging: "Do it". MEASURED ON THIS TYPE (SpoilerFleetProbe, SPOILER_FLEET=1). Authority is the pitching moment the stick's whole travel commands at 30 m/s with the wind turned to the body alpha asked for, as a fraction of its own alpha 0 value; the floor is the worst of it over alpha 10-60 at a 0.5 deg step. Floor 0.146 at alpha 40 -> 0.256 at alpha 40; alpha 45 0.199 -> 0.319. IT COSTS THE PITCH DAMPING NOTHING, and for a mechanical reason rather than a lucky one: the term carries sin(gain*deflEff) and is gated on a non-zero deflection, so it cannot appear in a controls-neutral quantity, and dM/dq is one. VERIFIED rather than asserted, because if it had moved then the gate would not be what we think it is: the worst dM/dq over alpha 10-60 is BIT-IDENTICAL at k 0 and k 0.6 on all eleven configs that gained it and on the two that already had it. Vso AND THE TRIM ARE UNMOVED TOO, which was not obvious and had to be measured rather than argued: unlike stabHighAlphaK's 60-90 deg band, this term opens at 10 deg of the strip's OWN flow, and a tail strip with the stick near its aft stop at the stall is not self-evidently below that. It is - measured on the Stearman at its own Vso, the stabiliser's local angle is 2.74 deg against the 10 deg onset, because the downwash (3.49 deg there) and the stabiliser's own negative incidence take it out of the body alpha - so the ramp never opens in any ordinary flight condition and every type's Vso, trim alpha and trim elevator come out unchanged to the digit. WHAT IT DOES CHANGE is high-alpha pitch authority and therefore the spin, which is the point, and nothing below the ramp.
spinAero.controlSpoilerOnsetDegSource: The spoiler ramp starts at the SECTION'S OWN STALL. 30 deg was chosen when every hStab was a naca0012 (stall 14 deg); a flat plate stalls at 9-12, which left alpha 20-34 with no table effectiveness and no spoiler yet - and that band WAS the hole in the elevator authority. Worth the whole difference: authority floor 0.165 at onset 30 against 0.249 at onset 10. Ty 2026-11-10 accepted the plate knowing this moves the term he judged the Pitts' spin on.

limits._vneSource: 98 mph IAS = 43.81 m/s (98 x 0.44704). FAA AFM for the SGS 2-33A at 1040 lb gross, which is also what this aeroplane's own painted FLIGHT LIMITS placard and its panel ASI red line read: NEVER EXCEED 98 MPH (tools/own_models/make_sgs_dials.py draws both -- the red tick at asi(98) and the placard text). TY'S DECISION 2026-11-10, asked which of the two numbers was wrong: "98 mph - the placard is right", on the reasoning he accepted -- the AFM figure and the painted placard agree with each other, and the config number had no source at all. SUPERSEDES vneMs 60 (134 mph), which entered in a September 2026 scaffolding commit with no citation and was never a 2-33 figure; it put the exterior flat dial's red line 36 mph above the red line painted on the same aeroplane's panel. WHAT MOVED WITH IT: the red line and scale that AsiDial derives (now the painted face declared below, so the two dials are one instrument), and the OverspeedBegan/Ended events in Sim/Replay/FlightEventLog, which read Limits.VneAt. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: LimitsConfig.LimitAt's VA-to-VNE load-factor ramp is inert on this type because it declares no vaMs (gMax/gMin hold to VNE), and the 1.1 x Vne dive speed that BladeElement.GovernorStops derives propeller pitch stops from cannot reach a glider -- propulsion is null, so there is no pitch stop, no windmill-restart speed (AircraftEngine's 0.9 x Vne) and no cached derived number that was calibrated against the old 134 mph. STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED HERE: the same placard reads MANEUVERING 65 MPH, MAX AERO TOW 98 MPH and MAX WINCH TOW 69 MPH. vaMs is left unset -- setting it without the AFM's load factors AT Vne would only make LimitAt interpolate between a number and itself, and what Va costs the pilot is Ty's call, not ours.

loading._comment: seats[].eye is the seated pilot's EYE (owner Ty, approved 2026-10-31), body frame +x fwd, +y right, +z DOWN, measured on extended gear; the Cockpit camera sits exactly there. The PRIMARY seat is first. loading.seats[].station, loading.tanks[] and loading.baggage[] are the arms from docs/pending/loading-arm-estimates.md (Codex lane, 2026-11-01): a published TCDS/POH arm where the row is CONFIRMED, converted to this frame through that aircraft's anchor. maxKg is the published placard where the source gives one. referenceKg is UNCHANGED and still follows the 172's convention, so the reference loading reproduces the authored mass, CG and inertia exactly and nothing moves at spawn. Whether each airframe's authored massKg includes a pilot or fuel is still the open W&B decision in AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.
loading._seatPlacardNote: maxKg is a CONVENTIONAL occupant placard (250 lb, and the J-3's own authored 300 lb), not a figure read from a POH. referenceKg follows the 172's convention: the primary seat carries the pilot that mass.massKg already includes, so the reference loading still reproduces the authored mass, CG and inertia exactly and nothing moves at spawn. Whether each airframe's authored massKg really includes a pilot is the open W&B decision in AGENT-LOG NEEDS YOU.

airspeed._unitsSource: TY'S EXPLICIT CALL. The 2-33's own panel ASI and its FLIGHT LIMITS placards are in mph (tools/own_models/make_sgs_dials.py, FAA AFM at 1040 lb: NEVER EXCEED 98 MPH).
airspeed._unitsRule: Ty 2026-11-10, asked what rule the other 27 types follow after settling five by hand, chose "by era and category": "Vintage, fabric and experimental types read mph; anything certified modern or turbine reads knots." FlyingGame.Core.Instruments.AsiUnits carries the rule and the exceptions.
airspeed._faceSource: THE FACE THIS AEROPLANE ALREADY WEARS, transcribed off the artwork rather than invented: tools/own_models/make_sgs_dials.py draws the 2-33's panel ASI as 20..160 mph over 15..345 deg (the photographed 2-33 dial), a green arc 38-65, a yellow arc 65-98 and the red tick at 98 -- all four 'FAA AFM 1040 lb markings' in that file. Declared here 2026-11-10 with the Vne correction above, because until now the config published only a unit and AsiDial DERIVED the exterior/flat dial off the spawn speed and limits.vneMs. That derivation was the vehicle for the bug: with vneMs 60 the flat dial read a red line at 134 mph while the panel dial 60 cm away read 98. Declaring the face does two things -- the exterior dial and the modelled panel become the same instrument (and the low-speed red arc now ends at the published 38 mph stall instead of at 0.62 x spawn = 30 mph), and the type comes under AsiUnitsTests.ADeclaredRedLineIsVneInTheDialsOwnUnit, which fails if the red line and limits.vneMs ever drift more than 3 % apart again. REJECTED: leaving the face derived. It would have worked (43.81 m/s x 2.2369 = 98.0 mph, so the red line lands right) but the scale top would have fallen to 140 while the painted face still says 160, re-opening the same disagreement one rung lower. NOTE FOR WHOEVER REDRAWS THE ART: make_sgs_dials.py still carries these numbers as its own literals -- unlike the four build.py faces it does not read this block. The two must be changed together until it does.
